Anatomy of a Hit

Interactive exploration of song length, danceability, tempo, and acousticness across 5,800+ Billboard hits.

The Shrinking Song: Duration Across Decades

Why are modern songs getting shorter? In the 1960s, 7-inch vinyl records limited songs to under 3 minutes. The CD revolution in the 1980s and 1990s unlocked epic 5-minute anthems. But since 2015, streaming royalty models (which pay per play once a listener passes 30 seconds) and short-form video on TikTok have pushed hit songs back down to historic lows.

The Rise of Danceability

Spotify’s danceability metric scores how suitable a track is for dancing based on tempo, rhythm stability, beat strength, and overall regularity. As drum machines, club synthesizers, and hip-hop 808s took over top-40 radio, the danceability of Billboard hits increased by over 25%.
